kind.description: What the task produces. code = source change proven by tests; check = a measurement or review with no product change; corpus = documents only. The done-contract compiler picks the oracle set and the red-first rule from this.

objective.description: One paragraph: what changes and why, readable without the plan.

ac_scope.description: AC ids of the governing spec this task claims. A new-symbol AC carries its own falsifier (path, find, replace, exit code) on the AC; the task only refs the id.

anchors.description: Files or directories the task changes (file_anchors).

issues_resolved.description: Issues this task resolves (for example #553); empty when it resolves none.

done_condition.description: The observable state that means done: a command and the output it must print, or a document state.

approach.description: Implementation notes: the route chosen and the traps already known.

write_set.description: Paths the claim may write. Optional: it defaults to anchors. Set it only when the claim must be wider or narrower than anchors.

red_waiver_reason.description: Why no red run precedes the implementation (a kind check or corpus task, or a change no test can observe red). Absent when red-first applies.

done_contract.description: Filled by the system when the task is approved; do not hand-write it. It is the compiled definition of done.

oracles.description: The oracles that must pass, each with its command and the AC it proves.

red_required.description: True when a runner-produced red run must be on record before done.

red_waiver_reason.description: Copied from red_waiver_reason when red_required is false.

contract_base.description: The commit the contract was compiled against.

execution_log_refs.description: References to the execution log: evidence versions, handoff ids, run ids. Appended during execution.

dimensions.question: What exactly can a reviewer observe to say this task is done, and which command or document state shows it?
How does the oracle go red before the implementation lands? If it cannot, state why and fill red_waiver_reason.
Which files may this task touch, and which nearby files must it leave alone?
Which claims or branches held by other sessions overlap these files, and what happens if one of them lands first?
If the task is blocked or must be abandoned, what is left behind and how is it undone?
